block_05_direct_answer.title: Direct answer
block_05_direct_answer.body_html: Choose a developer by matching delivery evidence and project quality to the specific purchase. For first-time buyers, review completed projects, delays, build quality, current project status, after-sales record and whether present commitments look realistic. Use official project records and completed developments rather than relying only on marketing reputation.

items.answer: Choose a developer by matching delivery evidence and project quality to the specific purchase. For first-time buyers, examine completed projects for delivery timing, build quality and whether finished results broadly match what buyers were originally promised.
items.question: How should I choose a developer?

items.answer: A developer check should focus on evidence of delivery, execution and accountability. Check repeated delays, unresolved defects, handover problems or other patterns that may be more informative than one successful project.
items.question: How should I assess a developer?

items.answer: Developer track record is best judged through completed projects and delivery behaviour. Assess whether construction stage, project updates and visible execution support the payment schedule and handover expectations being marketed.
items.question: How should I assess a developer's track record?

items.answer: Live availability can only be confirmed from a current sales or inventory source. Use a recent timestamp and identifiable source because inventory can change faster than most other project information.
items.question: How can I verify current availability?

items.answer: The best developer questions test the facts behind price, delivery and the contract. Important questions receive marketing language instead of specific project or contract information. Request documentary support for material answers rather than relying on verbal assurances.
